cards.name: Move Plane to Match Object
cards.summary: With an object that is already attached to the perspective grid selected, moves the matching grid plane (left, right or floor) to that object's depth or height, so the next art you draw or attach lands at the same plane position. The selected artwork itself does not change; only the grid plane moves.
use_for: adding windows, signs or posters at the same depth as an existing wall in a perspective street or interior scene
placing a second label on the same face of a packaging box drawn in perspective
lining up new perspective art with a shelf, step or floor tile that is already on the grid
avoid: moving the object rather than the plane: drag it with the Perspective Selection Tool
art that is not in perspective yet: there is nothing to match; attach it first with Object > Perspective > Attach to Active Plane
cards.how: Show the grid (View > Perspective Grid > Show Grid), select a perspective object with the Perspective Selection Tool, then choose the command. No dialog.
cards.script_api: No executeMenuCommand id was paired in the harvest; the menu item runs as Win32 WM_COMMAND 2147484341 posted to the Illustrator main window (menu path Object/Perspective/Move Plane to Match Object). The DOM has no plane-move call; it only offers doc.getPerspectiveActivePlane() / doc.setPerspectiveActivePlane(PerspectiveGridPlaneType.LEFTPLANE etc.) and PageItem.bringInPerspective(x, y, plane).

cards.name: Release with Perspective
cards.summary: Detaches the selected perspective objects from the perspective grid: they keep their current foreshortened shape but become ordinary artwork, so moving or scaling them no longer re-projects them onto a plane.
use_for: freezing finished perspective signage or packaging faces so later grid changes do not move them
reusing a foreshortened element (a sign, a window, a road marking) as a plain shape elsewhere in the layout
handing perspective art to tools that expect normal paths (envelope distort, pathfinder clean-up)
avoid: when more perspective edits are coming: keep it attached so it still snaps and re-projects
to get the flat, front-on art back: release keeps the distorted shape; keep an unattached copy before you attach art to the grid
cards.how: Select the perspective objects (Perspective Selection Tool or Selection Tool) and choose the command. No dialog.
cards.script_api: No executeMenuCommand id was paired in the harvest; the menu item runs as Win32 WM_COMMAND 2147484340 posted to the Illustrator main window (menu path Object/Perspective/Release with Perspective). No release-from-perspective call was found in the harvested DOM.

cards.name: Rasterize...
cards.summary: Permanently converts the selected vector objects (paths, live type, gradients, effects) into an embedded raster image at the resolution and colour model chosen in the Rasterize dialog. The result looks the same at that resolution but no longer edits as paths or text; Effect > Rasterize is the live, reversible version.
use_for: flattening a heavy illustration (blurs, meshes, many effects) so the file opens and prints reliably
locking a texture or photo-like vector so it cannot be edited further
preparing art for a raster-only destination at a resolution you control (e.g. a print resolution)
avoid: art you may still need to edit: use Effect > Rasterize (live) or keep a vector copy on a hidden layer
logos and type for print: rasterizing loses crisp vector edges at large sizes
producing a web or social image: export the artboard (File > Export) and keep the source vector
cards.how: Dialog: Color Model (RGB / CMYK / Grayscale / Bitmap, limited by the document colour mode); Resolution (Screen, Medium, High, Use Document Raster Effects Resolution, or Other); Background (White or Transparent); Anti-aliasing (None, Art Optimized, Type Optimized); Create Clipping Mask; Add N around object (padding).
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Rasterize 8 menu item") opens the Rasterize dialog (confirmed). Same job without the dialog: var o = new RasterizeOptions(); o.resolution = ppi; o.transparency = true; doc.rasterize(doc.selection, undefined, o). Document.rasterize(sourceArt, clipBounds, options) and RasterizeOptions (colorModel, resolution, transparency, antiAliasingMethod, clippingMask, padding ...) are in the harvested DOM (call unverified as written).

review.changes: how: dropped the Screen 72 / Medium 150 / High 300 ppi figures and use_for: the '300 ppi' example (neither is in the batch); script_api example now takes a ppi variable instead of a literal 300

cards.name: Grid
cards.summary: Turns the selected art into live Grid repeat art: copies of it tiled in rows and columns. On-canvas handles change the spacing and how many rows and columns show; grid types can offset alternate rows or columns by half (brick layouts) and flip rows or columns. Editing the source (double-click into isolation mode) updates every tile.
use_for: icon or logo background patterns for packaging, wrapping paper and social posts
evenly spaced ticket, badge or sticker sheets
textile and wallpaper pattern drafts that stay editable
avoid: a swatch you can apply as a fill to any shape: use Object > Pattern > Make
copies that each need different content: duplicate and transform them (Transform Again, Ctrl+D) or use Transform Each
cards.script_api: No executeMenuCommand id was paired in the harvest; the menu item runs as Win32 WM_COMMAND 2147484365 posted to the Illustrator main window (menu path Object/Repeat/Grid). Same result through the DOM: doc.gridRepeatItems.add(sourceArt, config) with a GridRepeatConfig (horizontalSpacing, verticalSpacing, patternType / rowFlipType / columnFlipType from RepeatGridShiftFlipType) (unverified).

review.changes: scriptable no -> partial: the menu item has no executeMenuCommand id, but the card's own harvested DOM route (doc.*RepeatItems.add / set*Configuration, unverified) produces the result, the same standard as the reviewed Slice Selection Tool card

cards.name: Mirror
cards.summary: Turns the selected art into live Mirror repeat art: a reflected copy appears across a symmetry axis that you can move and rotate on the canvas, and editing the source half in isolation mode updates the mirrored half as you draw.
use_for: symmetric logos, crests and emblems
faces, masks, butterflies, vases and other bilateral illustrations
ornaments and frames drawn one half at a time
avoid: a one-off flipped copy that never needs to update: Object > Transform > Reflect with Copy
more than two-fold symmetry: use Radial repeat
cards.script_api: No executeMenuCommand id was paired in the harvest; the menu item runs as Win32 WM_COMMAND 2147484366 posted to the Illustrator main window (menu path Object/Repeat/Mirror). Same result through the DOM: doc.symmetryRepeatItems.add(sourceArt, config) with a SymmetryRepeatConfig (axisRotationAngleInRadians) (unverified).

review.changes: scriptable no -> partial: the menu item has no executeMenuCommand id, but the card's own harvested DOM route (doc.*RepeatItems.add / set*Configuration, unverified) produces the result, the same standard as the reviewed Slice Selection Tool card

cards.name: Options...
cards.summary: Opens the Repeat Options dialog, the numeric settings for repeat art: for Radial the number of instances, radius and reverse overlapping; for Grid the horizontal and vertical spacing, grid type and row / column flips; and for Mirror the harvested DOM has only an axis angle (SymmetryRepeatConfig), so whether the dialog shows a Mirror section is not confirmed. Exactly which fields apply with or without repeat art selected was not confirmed by the harvest.
use_for: typing an exact number of petals, spokes or teeth into a radial motif
setting precise gutters between tiles of a grid repeat
matching repeat settings across several repeat objects in a pattern set
avoid: quick visual tweaks: drag the on-canvas repeat handles instead
objects that are not repeat art: make them a repeat first (Object > Repeat > Radial / Grid / Mirror)
cards.how: Dialog with Radial (number of instances, radius, reverse overlapping) and Grid (horizontal / vertical spacing, grid type, flip row / column) settings, named after the harvested RadialRepeatConfig / GridRepeatConfig fields (a Mirror section is not confirmed); the values apply to the selected repeat art.
cards.script_api: No executeMenuCommand id was paired in the harvest; the menu item runs as Win32 WM_COMMAND 2147484369 posted to the Illustrator main window (menu path Object/Repeat/Options...). DOM equivalent for selected repeat art: item.setRadialConfiguration(config, RadialRepeatUpdate.RADIALALL), item.setGridConfiguration(config, GridRepeatUpdate.GRIDALL) or item.setSymmetryConfiguration(config, SymmetryRepeatUpdate.SYMMETRYALL) (unverified).

review.changes: scriptable no -> partial: the menu item has no executeMenuCommand id, but the card's own harvested DOM route (doc.*RepeatItems.add / set*Configuration, unverified) produces the result, the same standard as the reviewed Slice Selection Tool card; summary / how: the Mirror section of the dialog was stated as fact, but nothing in the batch or the harvested DOM (SymmetryRepeatConfig has only axisRotationAngleInRadians) shows it; now hedged

cards.name: Radial
cards.summary: Turns the selected art into live Radial repeat art: copies arranged evenly around a circle, each rotated a step further round the centre. On-canvas handles set the radius and the number of instances and can open a gap in the ring; editing the source updates every copy.
use_for: mandalas, rosettes and flower motifs
clock faces, dials, gear rims and sunburst badges
circular logo marks, seals and stamps
avoid: type running around a circle: use Type on a Path
a fixed set of rotated copies that must be edited individually: Rotate dialog with Copy, then Transform Again (Ctrl+D)
cards.script_api: No executeMenuCommand id was paired in the harvest; the menu item runs as Win32 WM_COMMAND 2147484364 posted to the Illustrator main window (menu path Object/Repeat/Radial). Same result through the DOM: doc.radialRepeatItems.add(sourceArt, config) with a RadialRepeatConfig (numberOfInstances, radius, reverseOverlap) (unverified).

review.changes: scriptable no -> partial: the menu item has no executeMenuCommand id, but the card's own harvested DOM route (doc.*RepeatItems.add / set*Configuration, unverified) produces the result, the same standard as the reviewed Slice Selection Tool card

cards.name: Release
cards.summary: Releases the selected repeat art (radial, grid or mirror) back to ordinary art: the repeat stops, the live copies go away and the source artwork remains. To keep every copy as separate objects, use Object > Expand instead (behaviour from Adobe documentation, not checked in the harvest).
use_for: abandoning a repeat while keeping the motif drawn for it
starting over with a different repeat type on the same source art
avoid: keeping all the repeated copies as editable shapes: use Object > Expand
changing the count or spacing only: use Object > Repeat > Options or the on-canvas handles
cards.how: Select the repeat art and choose the command. No dialog.
cards.script_api: No executeMenuCommand id was paired in the harvest; the menu item runs as Win32 WM_COMMAND 2147484368 posted to the Illustrator main window (menu path Object/Repeat/Release). The harvested DOM has no release call (RadialRepeatItem / GridRepeatItem / SymmetryRepeatItem .remove() deletes the whole repeat art).

cards.name: Convert to Shape
cards.summary: Converts the selected regular paths into Live Shapes when their geometry is a rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse or polygon, giving them live corner widgets and editable shape properties (size, corner radius, sides) in the Properties / Transform panel. The look does not change; what happens to paths that match none of these shapes is not confirmed.
use_for: getting live, editable rounded corners on rectangles from older files or PDFs
making imported button and card rectangles resizable without distorting their corners
turning a drawn polygon back into one whose side count can be changed
avoid: freehand or complex outlines: they do not become live shapes; draw with the Rectangle / Ellipse / Polygon tools or the Shaper Tool
art you are about to edit point by point: that expands the live shape anyway
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Convert to Shape") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution).

cards.name: Expand Shape
cards.summary: Converts the selected Live Shapes (rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, polygons with live corners) into ordinary paths, dropping their shape properties and corner widgets; the outline stays exactly where it was.
use_for: freezing rounded corners before editing anchor points by hand
sending plain paths to a cutter, plotter, embroidery or older software
stopping corner widgets from getting in the way on dense icon art
avoid: shapes whose corner radius, size or side count may still change: keep the live shape
expanding strokes, effects or appearance: use Object > Expand or Object > Expand Appearance
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Expand Shape") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution).

cards.name: Show All
cards.summary: Makes every object that was hidden with Object > Hide visible again and selects the objects it reveals.
use_for: bringing back construction shapes hidden while working on a layout
checking a file before handoff or print for forgotten hidden art
restoring art hidden by a script or action
avoid: revealing a single object: click its eye in the Layers panel (Show All brings back everything)
final files where hidden art should go: delete it rather than hide it
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("showAll") (id paired by its shortcut, not confirmed by execution). DOM alternative: set item.hidden = false on each of doc.pageItems (unverified).

cards.name: Clip to Artboard
cards.summary: Toggles whether slicing is bounded by the artboard, so slices and the Save for Web (Legacy) slice table stop at the artboard edge instead of running to the bounds of all the artwork. The default state and how existing slices are trimmed were not confirmed.
use_for: web banner or email layouts sliced for Save for Web (Legacy) where only the artboard area should export
keeping off-artboard scraps out of a sliced export
avoid: modern asset export: use Export for Screens or the Asset Export panel
files that are not exported through Save for Web (Legacy): slicing has no effect on them
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AISlice Clip to Artboard") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution).

cards.name: Combine Slices
cards.summary: Merges the selected slices into one slice whose rectangle encloses the outer edges of all of them.
use_for: joining several small slices of a web layout into one image piece
cleaning up an over-sliced banner before Save for Web (Legacy)
avoid: grouping the artwork itself: slices only define export areas; group the art with Object > Group
modern asset export: use Export for Screens or the Asset Export panel
cards.how: Select two or more slices with the Slice Selection Tool, then choose the command. No dialog.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AISlice Combine") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution).

cards.name: Create from Guides
cards.summary: Creates slices from the document's ruler guides: the areas between the guides become slices for Save for Web (Legacy).
use_for: cutting a guide-based web or email layout into image pieces in one step
rows-and-columns slicing of a banner set up with guides
avoid: documents without guides: drag guides from the rulers first
modern asset export: use Export for Screens or the Asset Export panel
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AISlice Create from Guides") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution).

cards.name: Create from Selection
cards.summary: Creates slices from the bounds of the selected objects. Unlike Object > Slice > Make, these are user slices that are not tied to the art, so moving or resizing the objects later does not move the slices.
use_for: fixing export areas for a web layout whose art may still shift
slicing around a group of objects for Save for Web (Legacy)
avoid: slices that should follow the art when it changes: use Object > Slice > Make
modern asset export: use Export for Screens or the Asset Export panel
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AISlice Create from Selection") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution).

review.changes: status needs_input -> current: it needs only an ordinary selection of any art, the same as Object > Slice > Make (current) and the Transform dialogs; needs_input on this card set is kept for commands that need a slice, wrap, repeat or perspective object or guides to exist

cards.name: Delete All
cards.summary: Removes every slice in the document. Slices made with Object > Slice > Make are released rather than deleted, so the artwork itself stays.
use_for: clearing old web slices from a file reused for print
starting slicing again from scratch
avoid: removing one slice only: select it with the Slice Selection Tool and delete it, or Release it
files with no slices: the command does nothing
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AISlice Delete All Slices") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution).

cards.name: Divide Slices...
cards.summary: Splits the selected slice into a grid of smaller slices, either into a set number of equal slices or into slices of a set pixel size, horizontally and/or vertically.
use_for: cutting a large web image area into equal tiles
splitting a navigation bar slice into one slice per button
avoid: slices that must follow individual objects: use Object > Slice > Make on each object
modern asset export: use Export for Screens or the Asset Export panel
cards.how: Dialog: Divide Horizontally Into (N slices down, evenly spaced, or N pixels per slice) and Divide Vertically Into (N slices across, or N pixels per slice); Preview.

cards.name: Duplicate Slice

use_for: marking several equally sized image areas (thumbnails, buttons) in a web layout
avoid: duplicating the artwork: copy the art itself (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V or Alt-drag)
modern asset export: use Export for Screens or the Asset Export panel
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AISlice Duplicate") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution).

cards.name: Make
cards.summary: Makes a slice from each selected object, tied to the object's bounds: when the object moves or changes size, its slice follows. Slices define the image pieces written by Save for Web (Legacy).
use_for: marking buttons, banners and image areas of a web or email layout for sliced export
export areas that must stay matched to art that is still being edited
avoid: modern asset export: use Export for Screens or the Asset Export panel
a fixed export area independent of the art: use Object > Slice > Create from Selection
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AISlice Make Slice") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution). DOM alternative: item.sliced = true on the PageItem (unverified).

cards.name: Release
cards.summary: Removes the slice from the selected object made with Object > Slice > Make; the object itself is left untouched.
use_for: taking one element out of a sliced web layout while keeping the art
undoing an accidental Make Slice
avoid: removing every slice: Object > Slice > Delete All
user slices drawn with the Slice Tool: select and delete them
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AISlice Release Slice") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution). DOM alternative: item.sliced = false (unverified).

cards.name: Slice Options...
cards.summary: Opens Slice Options for the selected slice: what the slice becomes in a Save for Web (Legacy) HTML export (an image, an empty cell, or HTML text) and its web attributes such as name, link and alt text.
use_for: adding links and alt text to slices of an exported HTML email or web page
naming slice image files before a Save for Web (Legacy) export
avoid: modern asset export: use Export for Screens or the Asset Export panel
layouts that are not exported as sliced HTML: the options have no effect

cards.name: Make
cards.summary: Makes the selected object a text-wrap object: area text in the same layer flows around its shape, at the offset set in Text Wrap Options. Illustrator's help puts the wrap object above the text in the stacking order (the harvested DOM note for PageItem.wrapped words it the other way round; check on first use).
use_for: magazine-style layouts with body text flowing around a photo or cut-out
flyers and menus where copy wraps around an illustration
posters with text shaped around a logo or product shot
avoid: point text or type on a path: wrap only affects area text
text on a different layer from the object: move them into the same layer first
a plain rectangular column: size the area text frame or set columns instead
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Make Text Wrap") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution). DOM alternative: item.wrapped = true (with item.wrapOffset / item.wrapInside) (unverified).

cards.name: Release
cards.summary: Stops the selected object from pushing text away: the surrounding area text reflows as if the object were not there. The object itself is unchanged.
use_for: letting a decorative object overlap body text on purpose
removing a stale wrap after a layout change
avoid: changing the gap only: use Text Wrap Options
objects that are not wrap objects: the command does nothing
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Release Text Wrap") (id paired from the menu label, not confirmed by execution). DOM alternative: item.wrapped = false (unverified).

use_for: setting a consistent gutter between body text and photos in a brochure
pouring text inside a shape for a type-in-shape poster effect
avoid: quick text-in-a-shape: the Area Type Tool on the shape is simpler than an inverted wrap
